clue.text: Extremely civilised — second nature for new Assembly welcoming bishop

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them inside, so one piece goes into the other
a new assembly of something puts its parts together afresh, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
taken as written
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A newly formed parliament politely takes in a bishop, as if courtesy were second nature to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second nature' looks like a fixed phrase, but it is two pieces of fodder; the capital A on 'Assembly' disguises an ordinary anagram signal as a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means suave and courteous, so the superlative form describes someone at the very peak of polished manners.

clue.text: Edges away from crag by way of waterfall

indicators.note: taking the edges away strips off the outside letters and leaves only the inner part

parts.note: the inner letters of crag
in, as in 'in writing', means by way of or by means of

explanation.surface: A walker edges away from a cliff by way of a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waterfall' looks like a cascade on a cliff, but read it as two words: water that falls from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation dropping from clouds is literally water that falls, a cryptic split of the landscape word.

clue.text: It may be ducked by person facing Scotty?

definitions.text: It may be ducked by person facing Scotty?

parts.words: It may be ducked by person facing
parts.note: surface reading: a cricket delivery aimed at head height that the batter facing the bowler has to duck under
setter's reading: Scotty runs the transporter in Star Trek, so the person facing him is about to be beamed up

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a beamer is a dangerous full toss at the batter's head; the question mark lets 'Scotty' be either a bowler's nickname or the Star Trek engineer of 'Beam me up, Scotty'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a head-high full toss in cricket, which a batter avoids by bending low, and jokingly someone being transported.

clue.text: Where artist paints, to start with, eight landscapes in a row

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: what comes to start with is the opening letter of each word that follows

parts.note: the initial letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A painter at work on a sequence of eight landscapes hung side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: A tier is a row or rank, as in tiers of seating in a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is a studio or workshop, especially one used by a painter or designer.

clue.text: So to translate entails involving Italy?

definitions.text: So to translate entails involving Italy?

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or include, so one piece goes inside the other
to translate is to carry across into another form, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A question about whether translating a text means bringing Italy into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: putting something into the language of ancient Italy is what this word means.
explanation.definitionFit: To Latinise is to render something into Latin, the language that spread from Rome across Italy.

clue.text: Landlady perhaps after squat, this communication's from the heart

parts.note: squat is slang for nothing, and love is nil in tennis
a landlady lets rooms, so she is one who lets

explanation.surface: A note from a landlady about squatters turns out to be heartfelt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the landlady piece behind the squat piece. Squat in the sense 'diddly squat' means nothing at all, which is love in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic note written to a sweetheart is a message whose feelings come straight from the heart.

clue.text: Endless pursuit of cyclist, one that's seen at resort?

indicators.note: with no end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cyclist's pastime is riding a bike
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cyclist chases endlessly after someone spotted at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pursuit' looks like a chase, but here it means a hobby or activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-piece swimsuit is a common sight on beaches and around pools at holiday resorts, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Agreed rent for rotating deck

indicators.note: rotating moves things round in a loop, so letters from the front travel round to the back

parts.note: amen is said to show agreement
rent as the past participle of rend, meaning ripped

explanation.surface: A tenant agrees a rent for a revolving platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord, but it is the old past participle of rend. The joined pieces rotate so their first five letters go to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room is to adorn or decorate it, and ornament as a verb has that same sense of embellishing.

clue.text: Ringmaster accepts vocal contributions from Simon Mayo

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was master of the boxing ring
the vowels in the name Simon

explanation.surface: A circus ringmaster welcomes singers onto a radio show hosted by the presenter Simon Mayo.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon Mayo is a British radio presenter, so the name reads as one person; split it, and Mayo is the definition. 'Vocal' stands for vowels here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is short for mayonnaise, and aioli is a garlic mayonnaise from Provence, so it is a type of that sauce.

clue.text: Make listener listen, eventually?

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens

indicators.note: what comes eventually comes at the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of listen

explanation.surface: Someone forcing a reluctant audience to pay attention in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' looks like a verb meaning compel, but it is the definition in the sense of making money.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a living or a profit is to gain money through work, so make and earn are synonyms.

clue.text: The end for Amorim, United badly limited by a mixture of agencies

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the name

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the letters come out in a jumbled order

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for United in football team names
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football headline: the end for Manchester United's manager Ruben Amorim after a team limited by a mix of agents.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruben Amorim became Manchester United manager in 2024, so the clue reads like a sacking story. 'Agencies' stands in for media, means through which things are done.
explanation.definitionFit: Multimedia combines several media such as text, sound and video, and media are channels or means of communication.

clue.text: Position marker moving cover to cover point, finally

indicators.note: covering something means going over and around it, so one piece encloses another
letters that are moving get shifted about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what comes finally is at the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder shifted from cover to cover point, with a marker showing the position.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover and cover point are fielding positions in cricket, which makes the surface sound like a field placing. 'Finally' applies only to 'point'.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a position vector gives the location of a point relative to an origin, so it marks a position.

clue.text: Inspector stuck at sea, it seems, suggesting justice

indicators.note: something stuck at a place is lodged there, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: the open sea is the ocean
DI is a Detective Inspector in British police ranks

explanation.surface: A police inspector marooned at sea seems to be hoping for justice.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is rare: theodicy is the defence of God's justice in a world that contains evil, and this is its adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodicy vindicates divine goodness and fairness despite suffering, so something relating to it points towards God's righteousness.

clue.text: Sars, possibly — the same wide-ranging cases

indicators.note: to case something is to box it up, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: epic means vast in scope
idem is Latin for the same, used in references

explanation.surface: The Sars outbreak brought the same widespread cases everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like patients with a disease, which suits the Sars surface, but it is a verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sars caused a widespread outbreak in 2003, so it is an example of a disease spreading through a population.

clue.text: Still time to feed monkey one

indicators.note: food goes into a mouth, so feeding puts one piece inside another

parts.note: an ape is a primate, loosely a monkey
T is the abbreviation for time
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: There is still time to give one of the monkeys its food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning yet, but it is the definition as an adjective meaning calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still is calm and untroubled, the state of being tranquil with no disturbance.

clue.text: Picked up moving note from Aztec Empire's head

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: astir means up and about, in motion

indicators.note: taking one thing from another removes it

parts.note: taken as written
te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone overheard a stirring message from the leader of the Aztec Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts as a sound signal, but in a down clue it lifts the word upward. Removing the note leaves A, Z, C of Aztec.
explanation.definitionFit: A czaritsa was a Russian empress, a woman who ruled the Russian Empire or was the wife of the tsar.

clue.text: Attend cop-shop about clearing nonconformist

parts.note: to attend is to be at an event

indicators.note: clearing something out removes it

parts.note: nick is British slang for a police station
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to report to the police station about a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: A nick is British slang for a police station, here losing the abbreviation for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatniks were 1950s bohemians who rejected conventional society, so they are a type of social rebel.

clue.text: Man here one hears about, saving lives

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: saving something means keeping it safe within, so one piece holds the other
turned about means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to live is to be, so lives can mean is

explanation.surface: A lifeguard is the man here that people hear about, saving lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man, which lies between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is located in the stretch of water between Great Britain and Ireland, so this is a location definition.

clue.text: Good Beer Guide? CAMRA nut excluding English independent

indicators.note: excluding something leaves it out, so letters are dropped

parts.note: CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, so its fanatic is mad about ale
E is the abbreviation for English
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A real-ale enthusiast's guidebook to pubs, minus any English independent breweries.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMRA, the Campaign for Real Ale, is a British consumer group that publishes the Good Beer Guide every year.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual reference book, and this pub guide is published yearly, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Spooner's reported bad weather — this'll take blows up front

indicators.note: William Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: to report is to say; this word's opening sound is swapped with the next one's
hail is a kind of bad weather; its opening sound is swapped with the previous word's

explanation.surface: A forecaster reports a storm that will hit the front line first.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening consonants of the two words to get the answer. 'Blows' are gusts of wind, not punches.
explanation.definitionFit: A headsail is set forward of the foremast, so it catches the wind at the bow of a sailing boat.

clue.text: Avoid having key cut

parts.note: the Escape key on a keyboard
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Someone tries to avoid getting a new key cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like a door key being cut, but it is a computer key.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to deliberately abstain from or shun something, so it is a formal synonym for steer clear of.

clue.text: Root offered money for services when procuring Ashes?

indicators.note: to procure is to obtain and take in, so one piece gets another inside it

parts.note: a tip is money given for good service
the Ashes are kept in a small urn

explanation.surface: Joe Root, England's cricketer, being paid for his services in winning the Ashes.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Root is an England batter and the Ashes is the cricket series against Australia, whose trophy is a tiny urn; but 'Root' is the definition, a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a vegetable grown for its edible swollen taproot, so it is an example of a root crop.

clue.text: Bloodsucker is in Toulouse over and over again

indicators.note: turned over means upended, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: est is French for is, and Toulouse is in France
doing it again repeats the same piece a second time

explanation.surface: A mosquito bites over and over again in Toulouse.
explanation.walkthrough: A French city signals that 'is' must be translated into French. The reversed piece is repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse fly feeds on the blood of humans and animals and spreads sleeping sickness in Africa.

clue.text: Consuming carbon, bacteria fit local habitats

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is singular

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: E. coli is a common gut bacterium
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to mate is to fit together, as gears or parts do

explanation.surface: Microbes that feed on carbon are well suited to their local environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective meaning suited, but it is a verb meaning join together.
explanation.definitionFit: An ecoclimate is the set of climatic conditions in a particular ecological area, so it describes local living conditions.

clue.text: Marquetry left on centre of business counter

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so this piece is sent second
running counter means going the opposite way

parts.note: a hub is a centre of activity
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Inlaid woodwork is left on a shop counter in the middle of a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of business' looks like an instruction to take middle letters, but it is a synonym for hub, and 'counter' looks like a shop fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Buhl is decorative inlay of brass and tortoiseshell in furniture, named after the cabinetmaker Boulle, a kind of inlay work.

clue.text: From underneath, check Trump's derrière

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from underneath means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: to snub is to rebuff or check someone

explanation.surface: A tailor inspects the seat of Donald Trump's trousers from below.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump marks the definition as American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang buns are the buttocks, and derrière is a polite French-derived word for the backside.

clue.text: It's a surprise to 'ear from 'Arry Eliot

indicators.note: hearing it as a Cockney says it, with the h dropped, gives the sound to write down

parts.note: Heavens! is an exclamation of surprise, here without its h

explanation.surface: A Cockney called Harry is amazed to hear something about a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: George Eliot was the pen name of the novelist Mary Ann Evans. Cockney speech drops initial h, as the apostrophes show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian writer known as George Eliot was born with this surname, so the pen name stands for her real one.

clue.text: Who's missing when closing book on extended New Testament?

indicators.note: closing around something shuts it inside

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
B is the abbreviation for book
the letters NT written out in full as words

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is not present while the Bible is being closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extended' asks for the abbreviation NT spelt out letter by letter as the names of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is not present where expected, so it names the one missing.
